description: Issue #1178: the shared corpus for the change-set and bundle digests defined in apply-change-set-digest.md, beside this file. @clossys/launcher is tested against every case. Expected values were produced independently of the package: a stand-alone Python 3 script (standard library only) built each change set, computed its subject by removing changeSetDigest, branch, bundle, pullRequest and inverse and reducing every file whose derived member is true to its path, mode, derived, item and invariants, serialized it with json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')) -- which is RFC 8785 for these values, because every key is ASCII (so code-point order equals UTF-16 order) and every number is a small integer, both asserted by the script -- and hashed the UTF-8 bytes with hashlib.sha256. It then set branch, the title and changeSetDigest from that digest. Bundle digests were computed the same way over planDigest and the repositories sorted by id. The script also asserted every sameDigestAs and differsFrom relation below before writing this file. Arrays whose order carries no meaning were sorted as code rule C8 states. The briefs are each repository's projection of hubBrief (whose members are deliberately out of order), built by the same script from the brief contract's PER-REPOSITORY PROJECTION in its stated member order, serialized with json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) and one newline -- which writes the same bytes as JavaScript's JSON.stringify(value, null, 2): non-ASCII written as itself, and only the quotation mark, the backslash and control characters below U+0020 escaped -- and hashed as UTF-8. valid says whether the change set also passes the contract and its code rules; every change-set digest is defined either way. Hash inputs are placeholder text: no case is a real repository, package or plan.
